questions.question: Let $L[x]=x^{(n)}+a_{n-1}(t)x^{(n-1)}+\dots+a_0(t)x$ with coefficients continuous on $I$, let $S_0$ be the set of solutions of $L[x]=0$, and let $x_p$ be one solution of $L[x]=g$. Which set contains exactly all solutions of $L[x]=g$?
options: $\{x_p\}+S_0=\{x_p+h\colon\ h\in S_0\}$
$S_0$ itself, since $x_p$ is only one particular choice
$\{c\,x_p+h\colon\ c\in\mathbb{R},\ h\in S_0\}$
$\{x_p\}\cup S_0$, the particular and the homogeneous solutions

questions.question: The structure \"all solutions of $L[x]=g$ equal one solution plus all solutions of $L[x]=0$\" mirrors which fact about a linear system $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ from linear algebra?
options: The solutions of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ form a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$
Adding any vector of the column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$ to one solution gives all others
If $A\boldsymbol{x}_0=\boldsymbol{b}$, all solutions are $\{\boldsymbol{x}_0\}+\operatorname{Null}(A)$
$A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has exactly one solution for every $\boldsymbol{b}$

questions.question: Solutions $x_1,\dots,x_n$ of $L[x]=0$ (order $n$, coefficients continuous on $I$) are to be tested for being a basis of the solution space via their initial-data vectors $\big(x_i(t_0),\dots,x_i^{(n-1)}(t_0)\big)$. Which test is correct?
options: Check that these vectors are independent at one $t_0\in I$
Check that these vectors are independent at every $t\in I$ separately
Check that each $x_i(t)\neq0$ for every $t\in I$
Check that the values $x_1(t_0),\dots,x_n(t_0)$ are all different

questions.question: For the first-order equation $x'(t)=3x(t)-6$, the constant $x_p=2$ is a particular solution. Which formula, with an arbitrary constant $C$, gives all solutions?
options: $x(t)=-2+C\mathrm{e}^{3t}$
$x(t)=2+C\mathrm{e}^{-3t}$
$x(t)=C\big(2+\mathrm{e}^{3t}\big)$
$x(t)=2+C\mathrm{e}^{3t}$

questions.question: The function $2+\cos t$ solves $x''(t)+x(t)=2$, and $\cos t$, $\sin t$ solve $x''+x=0$. Which other function also solves $x''+x=2$?
options: $4+2\cos t$
$\cos t$
$2+5\sin t$

questions.question: For $x''+3x'+2x=4t$, the function $2t-3$ is a particular solution, and $\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ solves the homogeneous equation. Is $2t-3+2\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ also a particular solution of $x''+3x'+2x=4t$?
options: Yes; adding the homogeneous solution $2\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ keeps the forcing $4t$
No; a particular solution is unique once the forcing is fixed
No; it contains an exponential while the forcing $4t$ is polynomial
Yes, but only for $t\ge0$, where $2\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ stays bounded

questions.question: For $L[x]=x''+x$, suppose $L[x_a]=1$ and $L[x_b]=t$. Which combination solves $L[x]=3+2t$?
options: $x_a+x_b$

questions.question: Do $x_1(t)=\cos t$ and $x_2(t)=\sin\big(t+\tfrac\pi2\big)$, both solutions of $x''+x=0$, form a basis of its solution space?
options: Yes, since one is a cosine and the other a sine
No; $x_2=\cos t$, so their initial data at $0$ coincide
Yes, since the order is $2$ and there are two solutions
No, since $\sin\big(t+\tfrac\pi2\big)$ is not a solution

questions.question: For a linear operator $L$ and a forcing $g\not\equiv0$, why is the set of all solutions of $L[x]=g$ not a vector space, while $S_0$ (the solutions of $L[x]=0$) is?
options: The zero function is not a solution, since $L[0]=0\neq g$
Because the particular solution $x_p$ is not unique
Because the set has dimension $n+1$ instead of $n$
Because the set can be empty when $g$ is not continuous

questions.question: The function $\cos\big(t-\tfrac\pi3\big)$ solves $x''+x=0$, whose solution space has basis $\cos t,\sin t$. For which constants $c_1,c_2$ is $\cos\big(t-\tfrac\pi3\big)=c_1\cos t+c_2\sin t$ for all $t$?
options: No such constants exist; the three solutions are independent

questions.question: For $x''+x=\cos2t$, a particular solution is $-\tfrac{1}{3}\cos2t$ and the homogeneous solutions are $c_1\cos t+c_2\sin t$. Which solution satisfies $x(0)=0$ and $x'(0)=0$?
options: $x(t)=\tfrac{1}{3}\big(\cos2t-\cos t\big)$
$x(t)=\tfrac{t}{2}\sin t$
$x(t)=\tfrac{1}{3}\big(\cos t-\cos2t\big)$
$x(t)=\cos t-\cos2t$
